message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the Command Prompt**

If you’re running Windows and you want to terminate VS Code from a script or the console, you can use the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

---

### 1️⃣ Kill *all* VS Code processes

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – matches the image name (`code.exe`).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “End Process” in Task Manager).

This will immediately close every instance of VS Code that’s currently running.

---

### 2️⃣ Kill a specific VS Code process by PID

First, list the running processes to get the PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

You’ll see something like:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ ========= ============
code.exe                   12345 Console                    1     150,000 K
```

Then kill that particular PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

Replace `12345` with the actual PID you want to terminate.

---

### 3️⃣ Using PowerShell (optional)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can do the same thing with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or by PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force
```

---

#### ⚠️ Things to keep in mind

| Issue | What to watch out for |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Admin rights** | If VS Code was launched with elevated privileges, you may need to run the command prompt as Administrator. |
| **Unsaved work** | Force‑killing will not give VS Code a chance to autosave or prompt you about unsaved files. Use it only when you’re sure no important data will be lost. |
| **Multiple instances** | If you have several VS Code windows open, each runs under its own `code.exe` process. The `/IM` command kills all of them at once. |

---

### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Terminate all VS Code windows immediately. |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes and their PIDs. |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Terminate a specific VS Code window by PID. |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of `/IM`. |
| `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of `/PID`. |

That’s all there is to it—just hit the appropriate command and VS Code will exit. Happy scripting!
